items.title: Sick of Constant Pings, They’re Sending Texts at the Speed of Carrier Pigeon
items.author: Emmett Lindner
items.content: <article>Apps that let users send digital messages at ultraslow speeds have taken off, with users reveling in a slower pace of life. (Just don’t use the them to make dinner plans.)</article>

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg Buys an Irish Castle
items.author: Alan Yuhas
items.content: <article>The prominent landowner has added a nearly 200-year-old estate to his holdings. Archival information says it can take “a brisk walk of 4½ minutes to reach the dining room from the kitchen.”</article>

items.title: Anthropic Could Aim to Raise $100 Billion in Blockbuster I.P.O.
items.author: Sri Muppidi, Lauren Hirsch and Erin Griffith
items.content: <article>The offering could value the five-year-old A.I. start-up at $2 trillion, its bankers have told potential investors, which would exceed Elon Musk’s SpaceX.</article>

items.title: TikTok Settles With U.S. Over Child Privacy Concerns for $400 Million
items.author: David McCabe
items.content: <article>The Justice Department resolved a lawsuit that accused the social media company of illegally gathering children’s information.</article>

items.title: In China’s Biggest Car Recall, Tesla and 8 Others Will Address Door Safety
items.author: Keith Bradsher and Jack Ewing
items.content: <article>China’s regulator ordered changes after vehicle occupants sometimes had difficulty exiting electric cars, an issue that has led to lawsuits against Tesla in the United States.</article>

items.title: Voters Aren’t Waiting for November to Try Ousting Officials Over Data Centers
items.author: David McCabe
items.content: <article>As a backlash grows over data centers, more local officials are facing recall elections for their support of the computing sites.</article>

items.title: New Jersey Teenager Drops Bellwether Social Media Addiction Lawsuit
items.author: Eli Tan
items.content: <article>The case was the third of nine major personal injury cases that could expose Meta, YouTube, Snap and TikTok to financial damages and force them to change the designs of their platforms.</article>

items.title: AI Slop Is Everywhere. Spotify, LinkedIn and Others Have Had Enough.
items.author: Tiffany Hsu
items.content: <article>Spotify, LinkedIn and others are trying to dig out of a digital sewage heap full of low-quality content made with artificial intelligence.</article>

items.title: A County Got Rich From Data Centers. Some Question ‘At What Cost?’
items.author: Cecilia Kang and Caroline Gutman
items.content: <article>Loudoun County, Va., hosts more than 250 data centers that bring in huge tax revenues. But some officials and residents worry the county has become too dependent on that cash.</article>

items.title: OpenAI’s Two-Week Pause + Jill Lepore on the Threat of the “Artificial State” + Train of Thought
items.author: Kevin Roose, Casey Newton, Whitney Jones, Rachel Cohn, Vjeran Pavic, Katie McMurran, Dan Powell, Marion Lozano, Rowan Niemisto and Alyssa Moxley
items.content: <article>“It is the first time that we know of that a major lab has voluntarily slowed down.”</article>

items.title: Flock Cameras. Canoodling Lawyers. How Much Surveillance Are We Comfortable With?
items.author: Willy Staley
items.content: <article>Americans say they hate prying cameras. But they can’t look away.</article>

items.title: Two Binance Employees Detained in the U.A.E. Amid Police Inquiries
items.author: David Yaffe-Bellany and Michael Forsythe
items.content: <article>The detentions of the workers, who have been released, are a sign of legal pressure that the world’s largest crypto exchange faces in the Emirates, which is home to its main regulator.</article>

items.title: The Funny Way That Stand-Up Comics Are Posting on Social Media
items.author: Sopan Deb
items.content: <article>Comedians used to post footage of their performances to build a following. Now, some are finding that comic strip-style panels with captions pack a bigger punch.</article>

items.title: Chinese Start-Up Lands Reusable Rocket for the First Time
items.author: Adeel Hassan
items.content: <article>The milestone by the private company, LandSpace, could put China closer to challenging SpaceX’s rule in lower-cost spaceflight.</article>

items.title: Google’s Pixel 11 Comes With Plenty of A.I. Does Anyone Want That?
items.author: Brian X. Chen and Minh Connors
items.content: <article>The phone’s artificial intelligence can order groceries, book tables and take photos on a user’s behalf. But is it something people really want?</article>

items.title: Apple Removes Some Fees for App Developers in European Union
items.author: Kalley Huang
items.content: <article>The move followed a long battle with regulators over the company’s tight controls of its App Store.</article>

items.title: Meta to Stand Trial Over Claims It Addicted Children to Social Media
items.author: Cecilia Kang, Eli Tan and Emmy Martin
items.content: <article>California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey have taken the social media giant to trial in the first bellwether federal case over child harm.</article>

items.title: Silicon Valley Executives Are Tech Fans. Just Not For Their Own Kids.
items.author: David Streitfeld
items.content: <article>At home, moderation and restraint are the rule for tech parents. Boredom is exalted. Maybe they’re onto something.</article>

items.title: ICE Bars Its Workers From Wearing Meta’s Smart Glasses on the Job
items.author: Eli Tan and Hamed Aleaziz
items.content: <article>The agency joins a growing number of workplaces and groups to ban Meta’s devices, which have spurred privacy concerns.</article>

items.title: OpenAI Introduces ‘ChatGPT for Teens’ as Safety Concerns Grow
items.author: Cecilia Kang
items.content: <article>The artificial intelligence start-up announced a chatbot mode that will automatically limit some conversations to better protect young users.</article>

items.title: The Blackout That Could Devastate America
items.author: Christopher Cox
items.content: <article>The power grid relies on thousands of aging, hand-built transformers. If enough fail, the blackout could last years.</article>

items.title: Nvidia to Back Ohio Data Center With as Much as $105 Billion
items.author: Kalley Huang
items.content: <article>The data center, one of the world’s largest, could cost as much as $500 billion and will be leased by OpenAI.</article>
